title: Computer Science and Linux
weeks: Week 1: number systems, bits/bytes, CPU and memory hierarchy (Ch2).
Week 2: processes, threads, syscalls, user/kernel mode, stack/heap (Ch2).
Week 3: Linux shell, permissions, users, processes, packages (Ch3).
Week 4: Bash scripting, SSH, cron, logging; begin Python basics (Ch3, Ch5).
concepts: Chapters 1--3; *Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective* chapters 1--3.
reading: MIT OpenCourseWare introductory CS; OverTheWire Bandit levels 0--10.
courses: Linux man pages; Bash Guide; Python tutorial.
labs: Set up Ubuntu VM and Kali VM; practice 20 shell commands daily; complete Bandit levels 0--10.
programming: Write 5 Bash scripts; begin Python exercises (variables, loops, functions).
research: Keep a learning journal; document each command learned.
revision: Explain binary/hex conversion; draw process memory layout; list 10 Linux commands from memory.
criteria: Can navigate Linux fluently, explain CPU/memory concepts, and write simple scripts.

title: Networking
weeks: Week 1: OSI/TCP-IP, Ethernet, MAC, IP, CIDR/subnetting (Ch4).
Week 2: ARP, DNS, DHCP, ICMP; dig/traceroute (Ch4).
Week 3: TCP/UDP, ports, sockets, HTTP; Wireshark/tcpdump (Ch4, Ch8).
Week 4: TLS, proxies, NAT, firewalls; Nmap basics on lab network (Ch4).
concepts: Chapter 4; RFC 791/793/1034/9110 (skim); *Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach* ch1--3.
reading: Cisco Networking Academy intro; Wireshark user guide.
courses: IETF RFC Editor; Wireshark docs; Nmap reference.
labs: Capture a TCP handshake; run `dig +trace`; scan your own lab VM with Nmap.
programming: Write a Python DNS lookup tool and a URL parser (Ch5 projects 2--3).
research: Map your home network; document IP scheme and devices.
revision: Subnet 5 CIDR examples; explain TLS handshake; interpret a packet capture.
criteria: Can subnet, explain TCP/DNS/HTTP, and analyze basic captures.

title: Programming and Web Development
weeks: Week 1: Python data structures, functions, OOP, exceptions (Ch5).
Week 2: regex, files, JSON, HTTP requests, sockets (Ch5).
Week 3: HTML/CSS/JS, DOM, browser security model (Ch6).
Week 4: backend, REST, SQL, databases, Node/Express basics (Ch7).
concepts: Chapters 5--7; Python docs; MDN web docs.
reading: freeCodeCamp or MDN web tutorials; Python for Everybody (Coursera).
labs: Build the HTTP header analyzer, port scanner, and log analyzer (Ch5).
programming: Create a Flask/Express CRUD app with SQLite/Postgres; add authentication.
research: Write a blog post explaining SOP and CORS.
revision: Write a regex, a class, an HTTP request with timeout, and a parameterized SQL query.
criteria: Can build a small web app and explain client/server/data flow.

title: Web Security Foundations
weeks: Week 1: web architecture, request lifecycle, security headers (Ch8).
Week 2: OWASP Top 10:2025 categories A01--A05 (Ch9).
Week 3: A06--A10; XSS, CSRF, SQLi, SSRF deep dives (Ch9).
Week 4: Burp/ZAP workflows; certificate issues and auth failures (Ch9, Ch16).
concepts: Chapter 8--9; OWASP Top 10:2025; OWASP Web Testing Guide.
reading: PortSwigger Web Security Academy (first 20 labs); OWASP Juice Shop walkthroughs.
labs: PortSwigger labs: reflected/stored XSS, SQLi, CSRF; Juice Shop score 1-star.
programming: Build the XSS and SQLi demonstration labs (Ch29 projects 14--15).
research: Write notes on root cause and remediation for each lab solved.
revision: Explain 10 vulnerability classes with root cause and fix; solve 20 labs.
criteria: Can identify and explain common OWASP vulnerabilities; use Burp competently.

title: Bug Bounty Foundations
weeks: Week 1: programs, VDPs, disclosure, CVSS/CWE/CVE (Ch11).
Week 2: platforms, scope, rules of engagement (Ch12--13).
Week 3: recon methodology and tools (Ch14).
Week 4: manual testing methodology and case study (Ch15).
concepts: Chapters 11--15; ISO 29147 summary; platform policy pages.
reading: HackerOne/ Bugcrowd researcher docs; PortSwigger recon content.
courses: Official program policies; tool docs (Amass, subfinder, httpx).
labs: Recon your own domain; test a lab app end-to-end using the Ch15 method.
programming: Write the recon tool and inventory tool (Ch29 projects 1, 7).
research: Draft a report for a lab finding using Ch25 template.
revision: Parse a sample policy; identify scope, exclusions, restrictions; write 5 report summaries.
criteria: Can interpret a policy, perform safe recon, and write a clear report.

title: Advanced Web Security
weeks: Week 1: auth/authz logic, request smuggling theory (Ch10).
Week 2: caching, races, prototype pollution (Ch10).
Week 3: advanced SSRF, OAuth/JWT, WebSocket/GraphQL (Ch10, Ch17).
Week 4: business logic, multi-tenant, chains (Ch10, Ch17).
concepts: Chapter 10, 17; PortSwigger advanced labs; OWASP API Top 10.
reading: PortSwigger advanced labs (smuggling, races); crAPI labs.
labs: PortSwigger advanced labs; crAPI BOLA/BFLA; DVWA high level.
programming: Build GraphQL auth lab and race condition lab (Ch29 projects 18--19).
research: Write a chain analysis for a fictional scenario.
revision: Explain smuggling, cache poisoning, and a 3-step chain; solve 10 advanced labs.
criteria: Can reason about complex chains and advanced web/API flaws.

title: Cloud and Infrastructure Security
weeks: Week 1: cloud models, IAM, credentials, storage (Ch19).
Week 2: metadata services, serverless, containers (Ch19).
Week 3: Kubernetes, CI/CD, secrets, IaC (Ch19--20).
Week 4: supply chain, SBOM, auditing tools (Ch20, Ch16).
concepts: Chapters 19--20; AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar; CIS benchmarks.
reading: AWS Skill Builder free courses; Microsoft Learn cloud security; Prowler docs.
courses: Cloud provider docs; SLSA, SPDX, CycloneDX.
labs: Free-tier AWS lab: run Prowler, fix one finding; scan a lab container with Trivy.
programming: Build Docker security analyzer and IAM analyzer (Ch29 projects 20--21).
research: Write a Terraform misconfiguration example and check it with Checkov.
revision: Explain shared responsibility; find and fix 3 misconfigurations in your lab.
criteria: Can audit a lab cloud account and explain major cloud risks.

title: Mobile and API Security
weeks: Week 1: Android/iOS architecture, APK/IPA structure (Ch18).
Week 2: mobile storage, comms, deep links, pinning (Ch18).
Week 3: static/dynamic analysis with MobSF/JADX/Frida (Ch18).
Week 4: comprehensive API testing (Ch17).
concepts: Chapter 17--18; OWASP MASVS; OWASP API Top 10.
reading: OWASP MASVS training; MobSF docs; PortSwigger mobile content.
courses: Android developer security docs; OWASP API cheat sheets.
labs: Analyze a vulnerable lab APK with MobSF and JADX; crAPI full pass.
programming: Build Android analyzer and API testing framework (Ch29 projects 23, 6).
research: Document 10 mobile findings and 10 API findings with CWE mappings.
revision: Decompile an APK; capture mobile traffic via Burp; explain 5 API vulns.
criteria: Can perform basic mobile and API security assessments in a lab.

title: Advanced Security Research
weeks: Week 1: C memory, stack/heap, overflows (Ch21).
Week 2: mitigations, UAF, format strings; GDB (Ch21).
Week 3: reverse engineering, ELF/PE, Ghidra (Ch22).
Week 4: fuzzing, AFL++/libFuzzer, crash triage (Ch23).
concepts: Chapters 21--23; historical Phrack article; AFL++ docs.
labs: OverTheWire Narnia; build and fuzz a small parser; triage one crash.
programming: Build fuzzing harness and crash analysis tool (Ch29 projects 25--26).
research: Write a reverse-engineering walkthrough for a lab binary.
revision: Explain ASLR/NX/canaries; use GDB; triage a crash with ASan.
criteria: Can explain memory corruption, use a debugger, and run a basic fuzzing campaign.

title: AI and LLM Security
weeks: Week 1: ML/LLM architecture, transformers, embeddings (Ch24).
Week 2: RAG, agents, tool calling, memory (Ch24).
Week 3: OWASP LLM Top 10 2026 and Agentic Top 10 2026 (Ch24).
Week 4: AI tools, methodology, jailbreak vs. vuln (Ch24).
concepts: Chapter 24; OWASP LLM/Agentic Top 10 2026; MITRE ATLAS.
reading: OWASP GenAI resources; Promptfoo/Garak docs; local model setup.
labs: Lakera Gandalf; build a local RAG app with two tenants; test injection.
programming: Build RAG security framework, prompt injection evaluator, agent auditor (Ch29 projects 27--29).
research: Write an evaluation report distinguishing safety from security findings.
revision: Map an AI app to both OWASP lists; demonstrate one measurable security finding.
criteria: Can analyze AI systems for prompt injection, RAG isolation, and tool authorization.

title: Professional Bug Bounty Practice
weeks: Week 1: program selection, policy deep-dive, inventory (Ch26).
Week 2: manual testing on an authorized program or lab (Ch15).
Week 3: validation, impact, evidence, reporting (Ch25).
Week 4: triage communication, disclosure, portfolio (Ch25, Ch27).
concepts: Chapters 25--27; platform policies; public disclosures (where allowed).
reading: Platform researcher docs; OWASP disclosure guidance.
labs: Choose one authorized program; perform a full workflow; submit one high-quality report if a valid finding exists.
research: Publish one technical blog post and polish a GitHub repo.
revision: Write 3 full reports from lab findings; explain triage outcomes.
criteria: Can run the full workflow professionally; has a portfolio artifact.

title: Advanced Research and Specialization
weeks: Week 1: novel vulnerability research methodology; choose a niche.
Week 2: build a new tool or deepen a specialization.
Week 3: open-source contribution / responsible disclosure.
Week 4: portfolio review, roadmap revision, plan next year.
concepts: Chapters 28--35; chosen specialization papers and advisories.
reading: Security conferences/C TFtime events; advanced platform labs.
labs: Run a sustained research project in your niche; present or publish responsibly.
programming: Extend one portfolio tool with new features and tests.
research: Write a year-in-review and a 12-month specialization plan.
revision: Defend your research methodology; explain one deep finding end-to-end.
criteria: Has a demonstrable specialty, a public portfolio, and a concrete plan.
